main.description: badge.blue remote attestation proof record (https://badge.blue). Stored in the attestor's repository and referenced from the subject record's signatures array via com.atproto.repo.strongRef. The `cid` is the badge.blue attestation CID: the subject record (signatures stripped) with this record's metadata (cid/signature/signatures stripped, `repository` = subject's repo DID added) inserted as $sig, serialized to DAG-CBOR, SHA-256 hashed, wrapped as CIDv1 (dag-cbor codec). Verifiers recompute that CID and require it to match; copying the subject record to another repository changes the CID and invalidates the proof.

subject.description: Strong reference to the record being attested, so verifiers can fetch it and recompute the attestation CID.

cid.description: badge.blue attestation CID computed over the subject record, this record's metadata, and the subject's repository DID.

issuer.description: DID of the attesting party (e.g. the did:web of the service that minted this proof).

signatures.description: badge.blue attestations over this proof record itself (the attestor's inline signature).

inline.description: badge.blue inline attestation: an ECDSA signature over the attestation CID, embedded in the record's signatures array. The CID is computed from the record (signatures stripped), this entry's metadata (cid/signature stripped, `repository` = authoring repo DID added) inserted as $sig, DAG-CBOR + SHA-256 + CIDv1. Signatures are low-S normalized; supported curves are P-256 and K-256 (did:key).

key.description: did:key public-key reference used to verify the signature.

issuer.description: DID of the signing party (e.g. the did:web of the service holding the key). Verifiers may bind `key` to this DID's document when the authoring account's DID document does not list it.

cid.description: The computed badge.blue attestation CID (base32 CIDv1) this entry signs.

signature.description: Low-S normalized ECDSA signature over the CID bytes.

signatures.description: badge.blue signatures array: inline attestations and/or strongRefs to remote attestation proof records (com.publicdomainrelay.temp.market.attestation). Always stripped from the record before attestation-CID computation, so attaching attestations never changes the signing payload.
